subject: Invoice consolidation and VAT exemption handling for BrightWorks order form
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@brightworks.io>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Invoice flow proposal for your order form – request for tax docs

Hi Lisa,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. I chatted with Finance and Legal this morning and put together a simple proposal for how we can handle invoicing across BrightWorks' two purchasing entities without changing the signed MSA. High level:

- Consolidated monthly invoice to BrightWorks Group (preferred) OR split invoicing by entity if finance/legal require local remittance.
- If consolidated, BrightWorks would provide a single PO and we would route VAT responsibilities via their supplied tax residency certificate.
- If they require split invoices, we will accept per-entity invoicing but will need to adjust the order form to list invoice recipients and confirm net terms per entity.

Attached: BrightWorks_OrderForm_v3.pdf (proposed redline) and a checklist of items we need from your procurement team (tax cert, PO format, remit entity). Can you confirm which path Finance prefers?

If consolidated is acceptable, Marcus will follow up with the minor redlines to the order form (invoice recipient fields + billing contact) and Kimberly will draft the billing appendix for net terms and VAT handling.

Best,
Grace

--
Grace O'Connor
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
+1 415-555-0198

From: Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@brightworks.io>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: BrightWorks Finance <finance@brightworks.io>
Date: 2026-10-28T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Invoice flow proposal for your order form – request for tax docs

Thanks Grace — consolidated invoice would be easiest for our AP team, but our legal team is asking whether Redwood can accept a downstream VAT exemption for one of our EU entities (BrightWorks EU Ltd) while billing consolidated to BrightWorks Group. I attached the tax residency we have on file — is that sufficient?

Also: what do you need on the PO to make consolidated invoicing work for you (single remit address? entity id?)

Cheers,
Lisa

--
Lisa Chen
Procurement Manager
BrightWorks
lisa.chen@brightworks.io

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-29T08:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Invoice flow proposal — draft redlines attached

Grace / Kim — I pushed a tidy redline into BrightWorks_OrderForm_v3.pdf to add: invoice_recipient_name, remit_entity_tax_id, and billing_contact_email. Also annotated a fallback clause: if the customer requires split invoices, we add Appendix A listing entities + net terms per entity (Net30 default).

Proposed fallback language (short):
"If Customer requires separate invoices per legal entity, Seller will issue invoices to the entities listed in Appendix A. Customer acknowledges that separate invoicing may alter payment allocation and VAT treatment."

If we go consolidated and BrightWorks supplies the tax residency cert for EU exemption, Legal wants an explicit acceptance clause to avoid exposure: e.g., "Seller will rely on documents provided by Customer for VAT treatment; any liability arising from incorrect documentation will be reversed per Section X."

I can attach the annotated PDF to the HubSpot deal once we agree.

- Marcus

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@brightworks.io>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-30T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Invoice flow proposal — legal language for VAT reliance and net terms

Hi Lisa — thanks for the quick reply and for the tax cert. A few legal points to make this workable without redoing the MSA: 

1) VAT reliance clause: we can accept a customer-supplied tax residency / exemption certificate and will treat charges accordingly from the invoice date, provided Customer confirms accuracy in writing. If the certificate is later found invalid, we reserve the right to reissue corrected invoices and recover unpaid VAT.

2) Net terms handling: consolidated invoice -> single Net30 by default. If BrightWorks needs separate net terms per entity, we can include per-entity net terms in Appendix A, but that requires AP contact per entity and separate POs or a consolidated PO that clearly lists entity allocations.

3) PO requirements for consolidated invoices: please include (a) remit entity name for payment reconciliation, (b) tax ID for remit entity, and (c) a line stating "single monthly invoice for Redwood services, remit to BrightWorks Group".

Can you confirm whether Finance can provide a consolidated PO with those items? If not, we'll prepare the Appendix A split flow and show sample invoices for both flows so your AP can validate.

Best,
Kimberly

--
Kimberly Park
Sr. Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference

From: Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@brightworks.io>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-01T09:07:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Invoice flow proposal — legal language for VAT reliance and net terms

Kimberly — I'll escalate to Finance legal and get them to confirm they can provide a consolidated PO with the three required fields. They are inclined to keep single invoice (AP workload) but need written acceptance on reliance language. If legal signs off, we won't need Appendix A.

I expect confirmation by EOD Tuesday. Also, FYI, BrightWorks prefers Net45 for strategic vendors. Would Redwood consider Net45 on a consolidated invoice? If we do Net45, what does that mean for your billing cadence?

Thanks,
Lisa

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@brightworks.io>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-02T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Invoice flow proposal — summary and next steps

Lisa — perfect, thanks. To summarize next steps so we have a single action list: 

1) BrightWorks Legal: confirm acceptance of Redwood's VAT reliance clause in writing (email reply is fine).
2) BrightWorks Finance/AP: provide consolidated PO with remit_entity_name, remit_tax_id, billing_contact_email.
3) If BrightWorks wants Net45: Redwood can accept Net45 on consolidated invoices for this deal (BW-2026-0895) with a one-time activation: we will (a) run credit check on the consolidated remit entity, and (b) shift our billing cadence to produce invoice on the 1st of the month with due date 45 days after invoice date. This will be captured in the order form appendix.
4) If split invoicing is required: BrightWorks to provide PO per entity and we will deliver Appendix A; legal redlines will be required to the order form.

Once we have the written acceptance and PO, Marcus will upload the signed order form to DocuSign (I included the signing link in related_links) and Kimberly will issue the billing appendix to be attached to the order form.

I'll follow up after we receive your confirmation. Thanks again — we want to keep your AP process simple.

Best,
Grace

Attachments referenced: BrightWorks_OrderForm_v3.pdf (redline), Tax_Residency_Certificate.pdf
